app_tagline: Turn your Minecraft dye into as many stained-glass colors as possible, with counts as even as possible.
app_meta_description: Plan the mathematically optimal way to craft Minecraft dyes and stained glass from your inventory.
app_footer: Runs entirely in your browser. Recipe data: {version}.
section_inventory_description: The dye units and stained-glass blocks you already have.
section_craft_description: Recipe executions, in an order where every input is ready before it’s needed.
section_glass_description: Each glass dyeing uses 1 dye unit and 8 plain glass blocks, and gives 8 stained-glass blocks.
section_final_description: Stained-glass blocks per color after the plan.
section_leftovers_description: Dye units left after the plan.
inventory_keyboard_hint: Tab moves between fields. ↑/↓ step by 1, Shift+↑/↓ by 64, Enter applies.
input_error_empty: Enter a number, or 0 if you have none.
input_error_negative: Enter 0 or more. Negative amounts aren’t possible.
input_error_integer: Enter a whole number, like 12. Items can’t be split.
plain_glass_unlimited_hint: Turn off to enter how many plain glass blocks you have.
mode_balanced_description: Most colors first, then the most even counts.
mode_maximum_output_description: The most stained-glass blocks, balance aside.
mode_target_description: Reach a set count in the colors you pick.
confirm_sample_title: Replace your inventory with the sample?
confirm_sample_description: Your current dye units, stained-glass blocks and plain glass setting will be overwritten.
confirm_reset_description: Every count goes back to 0 and the options go back to their defaults.
toast_import_failed: Couldn’t import that file. Nothing was changed.
import_error_shape: The file isn’t a Dye Optimizer export.
import_error_count: {path} must be a whole number from 0 to {max} (found {value}).
results_error_title: The optimizer couldn’t produce a result
results_error_validation: The solver’s answer failed the integer checks, so it isn’t shown. Change the inventory or try again.
results_error_load: The solver couldn’t be loaded. Check your connection and reload the page.
results_invalid_input: Fix the highlighted fields to see a result.
results_empty_description: Enter your dye units or stained-glass blocks, or load the sample inventory.
metric_balance_floor_hint: Smallest final count among your colors
metric_spread_hint: Largest count minus the balance floor
table_hide_empty: Only colors in the final inventory are listed.
plan_no_recipes: No dye crafting needed: every color is dyed from dye you already have.
plan_no_glass: No glass dyeing in this plan.
recipe_dialog_source: Verified against the vanilla recipe file
leftovers_dialog_title: Why the plan leaves dye unused
leftovers_intro_balanced: Large leftovers can be intentional. The Balanced optimizer only spends dye when it keeps your colors even: spending hundreds of extra dye units on one color would make that color huge and ruin the balance.
leftovers_intro_maximum: Maximum output spends every dye unit it can. Anything left over couldn’t be used, usually because plain glass ran out.
leftovers_intro_target: Target mode only spends the dye your targets need, so the rest stays in your inventory.
leftovers_note_spread: {dye}: one more dye unit on glass would give {next} instead of {current}, above the largest count ({largest}), so the spread would grow.
leftovers_note_other: {dye}: using it wouldn’t add a color, raise the balance floor or reduce the spread.
bottleneck_none: Add some dye units or stained-glass blocks first.
bottleneck_heading: One smallest resource increase that would improve the result
bottleneck_required: {amount} required to raise every color above the current balance floor
bottleneck_unique: This is the only smallest increase (proven by re-solving without it).
bottleneck_not_unique: It isn’t the only option. These work just as well:
bottleneck_next_floor: With it, the balance floor could rise from {current} to at least {next}.
bottleneck_dialog_title: Why the balance floor stops at {floor}
bottleneck_dialog_intro: To raise the balance floor, every color in your final inventory needs at least {next} blocks. Glass comes 8 blocks per dye unit (S = E + 8·G), so a color’s next reachable count can be well above {next}.
bottleneck_dialog_conclusion: With your current inventory that next level is infeasible. The smallest extra starting resources that make it feasible are:
unreachable_description: You have no dye units or stained-glass blocks of these, and no recipe can make the dye from what you have.
target_unmet_unreachable: {color}: you have none and no recipe can make it from what you have.
target_unmet_short: {color}: {current}, {shortfall} short. Your resources run out before it gets there.
target_increase_heading: One smallest resource increase that would meet every target
